data.name: Brihadish
data.long_meaning: Brihadish is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Brihat', meaning 'extensive, large, or wide'. The suffix '-ish' denotes the one who possesses or rules over something. In Hindu mythology, Brihadish is considered the lord of the universe or the supreme deity, representing creation, preservation, and destruction.

historical_references.reference: Brihadishwas a renowned Hindu king of the Varmadeva dynasty in the 13th century CE. He ruled over the regions of present-day Maharashtra, India.

Another Brihadish, a prominent Jaina saint, lived during the 5th and 6th centuries CE. He was a disciple of Mahavira and is known for his teachings on ahimsa (non-violence) and the virtues of compassion and renunciation.
